1 · Intro

When to use it.

A salary change you enter in Oracle does not pay anyone by itself. It updates an element entry, and payroll picks that entry up in the payroll period it falls in.

Knowing how effective dates, the payroll cutoff, and retroactive pay interact lets you set expectations with employees.

Use this whenYou are entering or reviewing a pay change and need to know which paycheck it will hit.

2 · Walk through

How a pay change flows.

Check off each item as you read.

Which paycheck will it hit?
SituationTypical result
Approved before cutoff, effective this periodPaid this period
Approved after cutoff, effective this periodPaid next period with retro
Effective date in a past, paid periodRetro difference paid in a later run
Hourly rate change, non-exemptApplies to approved UKG hours in the period

Watch-outs

  • Pending approvals do not pay. A change still waiting in approvals at cutoff misses that payroll.
  • Retro only covers elements set up for retroactive pay. Do not promise a retro amount; payroll calculates it.
  • Open item: confirm with payroll which Vanderbilt earnings use Process separately and how retro shows on the payslip.

HCM Academy job aid · Compensation Management

Compensation impacts on payroll processing

Use when: You are entering or reviewing a pay change and need to know which paycheck it will hit. · System: Oracle HCM

  1. The salary basis decides how pay is stored.
  2. Saving a salary change writes the person's element entry.
  3. The effective date says when the pay is earned; the cutoff says when it is paid.
    • Check the payroll calendar, not memory
  4. Backdated changes pay through retroactive processing.
  5. Some earnings are set to Process separately.
  6. Confirm the result before payday.
